name: Root-grown hut
kind: Building shell with a door plate
status: Example. Exterior shell generated, scaled by its door, cleaned, and given a door plate, as a standard 3D model. No interior, not yet in Skyrim's model format and not in the game.
summary: A one-room dwelling of the interior, trained from living root and limb. It shows the buildings route for an organic shape: one generated shell, door included, with the door then found on the real geometry and covered by a plate that would carry the prompt.

need.why: Root pieces are held (ramps, roots, Hist trunks) but no root-grown hut was found in any mod we hold, by name or by looking. The Root-Folk's 19 places have 3 source interiors between them for 22 households.
need.lore: "The interior does not build a house, it trains one. Root and canopy limb are grafted, bent and tied over years into wall, floor, stair and threshold while still alive"; sealed with Hist-sap resin, roofed in bark shingle and layered canopy leaf, never reed thatch, no stone (story/lore/topics/material-culture.md, the grown-root kit).
need.use: Swapped in for a source building at the adapting stage of a Root-Folk place draft, its door on the source door's position, with an interior behind it.

brief.text: A rounded, slightly lopsided dome of thick grafted roots, gaps sealed with amber sap, a roof of bark shingle and broad leaves, one low arched plank door, two round sap windows. No stone, thatch, stilts, metal, ropes, hanging things or thin root tendrils.

fees.note: From Fal's list prices as read on 24 November, not from a bill.
lines: 1 image edit (painted concept to a photograph, tendrils removed)

stages.name: 1. Reference images
stages.did: Two images from one brief, three-quarter view from the front. Both came back as painted concept art with thin root tendrils spreading over a patch of ground. The better one was then edited into a photograph of the same building with the tendrils and ground removed.
stages.looked: Both read at once as a root-grown hut and match the lore: grafted roots, sap windows, bark and leaf roof, no stone. The first shows its plank door clearly; the second half hides it. As paintings they would bake a painted look into the model, and the tendrils are the canoe's rope again.
stages.decision: Reference 1, edited. Lesson for the brief: ask for a photograph of a physical object by name, and for a flat clean base.
images: Reference 1 as a photograph, tendrils and ground removed: the image the model was made from

stages.name: 2. Generation
stages.verdict: pass at the first try: H3.1 kept
stages.did: The edited image to Tripo H3.1 and Tripo P2, each asked for at most 40,000 triangles.
stages.looked: Both are the hut, from every side: the generator invented a believable back with more roots and sap windows. H3.1 is closed underneath. P2 came back as a hollow shell open at the base, in 226 pieces, with a glossier, wetter look.
stages.decision: H3.1 kept: nearly one closed piece (4 open edges against 7,223).
images: Tripo P2: hollow and in pieces

stages.name: 3. Shaping and clean-up
stages.did: Two loose pieces removed. The whole shell was scaled so that its door is 2.3 m high, since a building's size has to follow its door, then turned so the door faces forward and stood on the ground. Triangles cut from 39,104 to 14,000 with the texture layout kept.
stages.looked: The cut to 14,000 triangles does not show from the six views. At this size the hut is 8.9 m across and 5.5 m high: larger than the 6 m of the brief, but in line with King of the Murkmire's mud hut, which is about 10 m by 13 m.
stages.decision: Kept. Open point: one texture over a building this size gives about 240 pixels per metre, which is soft at arm's length. This is the size problem the plan answers with repeating materials; it has not been done on this example, so walk up to the wall in the viewer and judge it.

stages.name: 4. The door plate
stages.verdict: pass on the third attempt, with one open point
stages.did: The painted door was found on the real geometry: the largest flat patch facing outward at ground level, then grown over the neighbouring faces at the same depth to take in the whole door. A plate was made to that outline, 2 cm thick and 4 cm in front of the door, and an arrival point set 1.3 m out. In the game the plate would be invisible and carry the prompt; here it is drawn in orange.
stages.looked: First attempt: the plate covered a single plank, 0.73 m wide, because the grooves between planks broke the flat patch. Second attempt, with looser limits: the plate landed on a flat stretch of wall on another side of the hut, nowhere near the door. Third attempt, growing outward from the strict match: the plate sits in the doorway and reaches the ground.
stages.decision: Kept. Open point: the door's cross-bar and sill stand out further than the plate, so a crosshair aimed low would meet the bar first. The plate should stand in front of the furthest part of the doorway; that is the next hand step. The door is also narrower and lower than a vanilla house door.
images: The shell with its door plate and arrival point in orange

stages.name: 5. Interior and the game
stages.decision: Still owed: a matching interior of one or more rooms; collision a player can walk against; a distant-view model; repeating bark, sap and shingle materials so the wall is sharp up close; Skyrim's model format; one swap into a Root-Folk place draft; your look in game.
